question: Which organisms have been shown to make PHB from hydrolysates that contain xylose, and what feedstock did each study use?

claims.text: A Pseudomonas putida and Escherichia coli consortium converted lignocellulosic hydrolysate containing glucose and xylose into medium-chain-length PHA, not PHB, so it does not count as a PHB example.

gaps: For the pineapple core study, the retrieved text does not show whether strain A-04 consumed xylose from the hydrolysate or whether the PHB came only from glucose and fructose; the xylose consumption data are needed.

No primary paper on Paraburkholderia sacchari with a hydrolysate was retrieved; the wood-hydrolysate result is known only from a review's description, and the primary Dietrich et al. study and its sugar composition are absent from the corpus.
No record gives the xylose concentration in the wood hydrolysate used for Paraburkholderia sacchari.
The sunflower stalk titre and content records lack a stated strain or conditions field, so the feedstock-to-strain mapping relies on the passage text.

Only a few xylose-containing hydrolysate PHB studies were found; the search did not establish whether other organisms (e.g. Bacillus, Pseudomonas, or wild-type Paraburkholderia strains on corn stover, bagasse or similar feedstocks) have been reported.
Yields on xylose in the hydrolysate studies were not compared on a common basis, and the tool gave no yield ceiling for PHB from xylose in the corpus.
